name: AI incidents & governance
summary: US charges three over a $129m deepfake executive fraud; no AI attack on critical infrastructure found
state: On 6 Nov US prosecutors charged three men accused of using AI-generated voices and images of chief executives and lawyers to take more than $129m from businesses (ITPro; Greek City Times, 8 Nov). Searches on 17 Nov found no newer AI misuse incident of that scale, no AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure and no AI-attributed mass harm, so a significant AI misuse incident keeps this at Watch.
for_you: Deepfake fraud mainly targets businesses through faked calls or video from senior staff. Action Fraud and the NCSC publish guidance on verifying payment requests through a separate, known channel.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant AI misuse incident ($129m deepfake executive fraud charged 6 Nov)

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
